similar_scenes.name: Reacción rockista y new americana
similar_scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
similar_scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
similar_scenes.desc: Contra las «bandas inglesas con peinados raros», el regreso de la autenticidad: Rolling Stone denuncia que MTV vendió el rock'n'roll, Greil Marcus y Dave Marsh acusan al new pop de vacuidad e imperialismo británico. Antiguos punks se disfrazan de sureños alcohólicos (The Blasters, Violent Femmes, The Gun Club, Lone Justice, Blood on the Saddle) y triunfan Springsteen, Mellencamp y Fogerty. Pero Prince, «Beat It», ZZ Top, Van Halen o los remixes de Arthur Baker para Born in the U.S.A. aprenden del new pop; a la larga el hip hop heredará las fantasías de rebelión callejera.

similar_scenes.name: New wave americana
similar_scenes.book: Loops 1 y 2. Una historia de la música electrónica
similar_scenes.author: Javier Blánquez (ed.)
similar_scenes.desc: La new wave culta, sin prejuicios raciales, abre la puerta al dub y los ritmos negros: Devo y su «devolución» kraftwerkiana; Blondie, que coquetea con la disco y con Moroder; Talking Heads y sus sonidos de raíz; los B-52’s psicotrónicos; y el reverso maldito de San Francisco, Tuxedomoon y The Residents.

podcast.title: "Island of Misfit Toys"
podcast.body: Brandy Carlisle poetically referred to Americana music as "the island of the misfit toys," suggesting it provides a home for artists who feel they don't quite belong in more rigidly defined genres. "She wrote, Americana music is the island of the misfit toys. I am such a misfit."

podcast.title: Blending of Genres
podcast.body: Americana is described as a musical style that blends country, folk, blues, and rock, with a "slight dusting of alternative pixie dust," implying an indie or alternative sensibility infused into traditional roots music. "There's Americana, a blending of country, folk blues and rock, and then given a slight dusting of alternative pixie dust."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 7: All the rest

podcast.title: Community and Identity
podcast.body: Brandy Carlisle described Americana as "more than a genre," emphasizing its identity as a community, particularly for artists who might not fit neatly into other traditional categories. "Carlisle wrote on her Instagram post that Americana was more than a genre. It is a community and that is the genre that she had hoped that her song would be included in when considered for her Grammy."

podcast.title: John Mellencamp's Imperial Use
podcast.body: Indiana rocker John Mellencamp (then John Cougar Mellencamp) infused his hits with Americana and country-adjacent tropes, deepening this focus during his imperial peak with the 1987 album "The Lonesome Jubilee," which employed folk and country instruments like auto harp, banjo, accordion, and fiddle. This enabled him to successfully chart "rootsy folk rock" like "Paper in Fire" in a pop-dominated era. "had long infused his hits with Americana and even country adjacent tropes from Herz so good to pink houses, Jack and Diane to small town."

podcast.title: Not a Genre in the 1970s
podcast.body: The genre of Americana, as understood in contemporary music classification (e.g., for Grammy nominations), did not exist as a defined category in the 1970s. "when the Grammys told Brandy Carlyle that her song is not Americana enough, which was not even a genre in the 70s, and Casey Musgrave that her whole album is not country enough, the artists were quick to reassure their fans that they were not the ones abandoning their chosen communities."
